claim: People do notice anomalies and give them more attention than expected results; the failure is in what follows (explaining away, local patching), not in noticing. Re-opened: Trickett 2001 (3 scientists, anomalies 7.6 vs 1.5 later references in astronomy) and Meister 2021 (N=11, 46 anomaly situations, 20 explained by method error, 2 changed assumptions).
agent_test: Plant 1 odd datum in 20 tasks. Score noticing rate (is it mentioned) separately from response (patch vs reframe) at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: Trickett is 3 scientists in two datasets and Meister 11 pre-service teachers, so 'people' is a broad generalisation; the 7.6 vs 1.5 figure is astronomy only (physics 3.0 vs 1.25).

claim: Anomalies are mostly handled by local patching from the data display, not by revising the domain theory; theory change is the rare response in the Chinn and Brewer set. Still unverified: the 1998 response frequencies were not reachable (publisher 403). Small human data (Meister 2021, N=11) agree: 20 of 46 anomalies explained as method error, 2 changed assumptions; but conflicts with an own built model led to model change in 6 of 14.
agent_test: Code agent responses to a planted anomaly with the 7-way Chinn-Brewer scheme; compare base vs a schema that forces a 'what would make my frame wrong' step.

claim: Data that conflict with a plausible prior theory are down-weighted (treated as error) while the same data under an implausible theory are weighted more.
agent_test: Same evidence with a plausible vs implausible stated hypothesis; measure update size. Fugelsang N=14 only; Lord 1979 not opened.

claim: A symptom relief or a pass after an action is read as proof of the action (co-occurrence); in Kegworth this cemented the wrong engine shutdown for about 20 minutes.
agent_test: Tasks where a wrong fix gives a transient pass; count how often the agent closes the case without a check that could have failed.

claim: Salient distracting findings placed at the start or at the end of a case both cut medical students' diagnostic accuracy (0.269 to 0.110 and 0.168); the accuracy difference between early and late was not significant, but only early distractors shortened reading time per word, which the authors read as premature closure (single study, 58 students).
agent_test: Put a red herring at start vs end of the same prompt; measure accuracy at equal tokens.
audit_note: Al Essa et al. report accuracy 0.110 (early) vs 0.168 (late) but the pairwise contrast between early and late distractors was not significant; only reading time per word fell for early distractors.
claim_before_audit: Early salient distractors cut diagnostic accuracy more than late ones (premature closure by order).

claim: Corrections that give an alternative explanation reduce continued influence far more than a bare retraction, but rarely remove it fully.
agent_test: When the agent drops a hypothesis, require a replacement cause before it may discard the old one; compare lingering use of the dropped claim.
audit_note: Minor: Kan et al. found full elimination in their direct+alternative condition (score equal to baseline) and Mickelberg found full discounting of person misinformation in 2 of 3 experiments, so 'rarely remove it fully' holds for the literature as the authors frame it, not for every condition; Chan et al. meta-analysis not opened.

claim: The backfire effect (corrections strengthening the false belief) is not supported: a large replication found none.
agent_test: None needed; do not design the schema around backfire.

claim: Without an external signal, LLM intrinsic self-correction does not improve and often lowers accuracy; reported gains came from oracle stopping. New: s1 (budget forcing with 'Wait') raised AIME24 from 50.0 to up to 57.6 without an external signal; Cheng 2026 shows that telling a model its own draft is wrong does not remove the draft's pull. SPARC (d18) is theory fitted to Tsui, not a replication.
agent_test: Compare self-review vs external check (test, tool, retrieval) at equal tokens. Contested: Tsui shows a 'Wait' marker helps non-reasoning models; Huang tested reasoning models little.

claim: Models correct an error placed in the user's turn much more often than the same error in their own earlier output (blind spot 64.5% over 14 models); a single appended 'Wait' cuts it 89.3%. A neutral 'Wait' continuation also helped s1-32B on AIME24 (50.0 up to 57.6), but that spends more tokens and is a different task.
agent_test: Re-present own earlier step as 'a colleague's step' before review; compare with 'Wait'.

claim: When only counter-evidence is given and it is coherent, LLMs accept it; when prior-consistent evidence is also present, they favour it (GPT-4 about 80% on popular questions), and order changes answers.
agent_test: Shuffle evidence order and balance supportive vs conflicting items; measure answer flip rate. Xie plus the knowledge-conflict survey agree in direction.
audit_note: All four supporting lines are the same Xie et al. 2024 paper (arXiv 2305.13300) and the fifth, a survey, gives no numbers; the numbers themselves (GPT-4 about 80% memorization on most popular questions, order sensitivity, coherent single-source counter-evidence accepted) do match the paper.

claim: Models adopt wrong retrieved context over a correct prior more than 60% of the time; adoption falls as the context deviates more from truth and as model prior confidence rises.
agent_test: Inject wrong tool or retrieval output with graded deviation; test a 'state your own answer first, then compare' step (Astute-RAG style).

claim: Models commit early in multi-turn or staged information and do not recover: 39% average drop, unreliability +112%, aptitude -15%; restating info recovers only 15-20% (SNOWBALL); lower temperature does not fix it. Second source: MINT (1,035 cases, 11 LLMs): over 55% of answers committed in the first two turns, average accuracy loss 24.2%, instruction to wait did not stop it (guess rate before any evidence 99.9% for Med42-70B, 3.7% for Claude Sonnet 4.6).
agent_test: Present same facts staged vs all at once; add a 'discard draft and re-derive from all facts' operator and compare at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: Snowball's 15-20% is the share of the full-to-sharded drop mitigated (GPT-4o and 4o-mini, four tasks) and MINT's 24.2% is the average accuracy drop from early answering in a medical benchmark, not the same measure as Laban's 39%.

claim: Say: 91% of reasoning traces scored above threshold, yet reasoning score correlated only moderately with accuracy (R=0.56) versus R=0.69 for information utilization; the 65.6% (212/323) and 57% to 26% figures are correct.
agent_test: Staged-evidence tasks: log whether new data are used; test a forced 'which new datum contradicts my lead' step.
audit_note: The paper's body reports reasoning-rubric (R-IDEA) scores positively correlated with accuracy (R=0.56, p=0.02, 'moderate'); only the abstract says 'decorrelated', so 'did not predict correctness' is too strong.
claim_before_audit: Early diagnostic errors persist in staged information-seeking: 65.6% of wrong R1 diagnoses stayed wrong at R3 (32 models); information utilization fell 57% to 26%; good-looking reasoning (91% above threshold) did not predict correctness.

claim: Models rarely abstain or ask for clarification when the correct option is missing or the case is underspecified but looks low risk (false action about 70%); a short safety prompt cuts it to about 48% but not to zero. Agent-tool evidence agrees: AgentAbstain best paired accuracy 59.5% (act 90% vs abstain 41% in one scenario); Agentic Abstention: some agents never abstain, others abstain late; the safety-prompt figure itself is still from one paper.
agent_test: Items with no valid answer; measure commit rate with and without an explicit 'none fits' operator at equal tokens, and cost on answerable items.
audit_note: Minor: 'about 70%' is the mean false-action rate on no-correct-option medical MCQs (range 55-81% by model), and the 41% abstain vs 90% act figure is one scenario (S3) for the aggregate, not best agent.

claim: Red-herring and Einstellung benchmarks show LLMs fixated by familiar patterns (physicians 66% vs best models about 50% in 2025), but strong reasoning models reached physician level a year later; the gap is not permanent.
agent_test: Run Einstellung items on our agent with reasoning on and off; fixation may depend on reasoning mode.

claim: Models weigh in-context claims by how credible the source looks (adoption rose with stated source accuracy 20/50/90%), not by whether the claim is true. Anti-sycophancy prompts and steering lowered adoption of a credible source's claim together with adoption of the user's, with the two drops correlated (Pearson 0.87 across frontier models), so useful updating falls along with harmful. An explicit authority-limiting frame cut misleading-clue flips from 49.8% (TOOL) to 19.1% (TOOL+ANTIDOTE), cross-model mean on high-prior cases with no tool executed. For tool outputs, mean adoption of corrupted returns was 68.0% (search), 40.1% (sub-agent), 35.5% (code); a verify-by-tool-call prompt cut adoption modestly with little loss on correct returns, and a compare-with-prior-knowledge prompt cut adoption more for search and sub-agent tools but lowered accuracy on correct returns there.
agent_test: Misleading tool output with and without a 'tool output is evidence, not authority' frame; also measure loss of valid updates.
audit_note: Shapira et al. report that anti-sycophancy prompts/steering lowered adoption of the source's claim along with the user's and that the two drops correlate (Pearson 0.87), not that useful and harmful updating fell by about the same amount; also the COMPARE prompt cut adoption more than VERIFY only for search and sub-agent (code: 31.2 vs 30.4, no accuracy loss).
claim_before_audit: Source credibility, not truth, drives LLM updating; anti-sycophancy prompts cut useful updating about as much as harmful updating. An explicit authority-limiting frame cuts misleading-clue flips (49.8% to 19.1%). For tool outputs: mean adoption of corrupted returns 68.0% (search), 40.1% (sub-agent), 35.5% (code); a verify-by-tool-call prompt cut adoption with little loss on correct returns; a 'compare with prior knowledge' prompt cut it more but lowered accuracy on correct returns.

claim: Confirming tests lose and disconfirming tests win in a 2-4-6 style game; positive test strategy is not always bad (Klayman and Ha). FalsifyBench (12 LLMs, 1,200 games) is correlational: confirmation bias vs success rho -0.779; no forced-test arm.
agent_test: Rule-discovery tasks: require one test the current rule predicts to fail; compare success.

claim: Bias-targeted prompts (CoT, ignore-the-anchor, reflection) do not remove anchoring in GPT-4; ignore-irrelevant instructions only partly help.
agent_test: Anchor test with both-anchors strategy versus single instruction at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: Shi et al. tested distractor sentences in math word problems on GPT-3.5-era models, not anchoring, so 'partly help' is evidence about irrelevant context in general; Lou and Sun tested only GPT-4/GPT-4o.

claim: Role-split debate (devil's advocate, tutor against closure) recovered diagnoses from wrong first answers 71.3% (57/80) in GPT-4, but cases were picked for first-diagnosis failure and there is no control arm.
agent_test: Same-token control: self-consistency vs devil's advocate role; Huang found debate no better than self-consistency.

claim: Structured reflection and 'consider the opposite' reduce human bias but gains are small and measured in vignettes.
agent_test: Seen only as search summaries; re-check before use.

claim: Reasoning models show cognitive inertia (wrong readings that persist, loops of self-checks); a latent-update method reduced tokens and raised accuracy on small open models.
agent_test: Small models only (1.5B-7B); test before assuming it generalises to frontier agents.

claim: Fixation in anaesthesia simulation is common, but rates depend on the denominator: Schwid and O'Donnell 1992, 63% of 30 subjects made at least one fixation error; DeAnda and Gaba 1990, 20.5% (27 of 132) of unplanned incidents in 19 resident simulations. The Rudolph figure (about 23% correct diagnosis) remains an unverified conference-abstract snippet. Abstracts only were opened.
agent_test: Report fixation per run and per incident, never mixed. Do not use Rudolph's number.
audit_note: Minor: both checked from PubMed abstracts only (as the claim states); the two figures use different denominators (subjects vs incidents), as the claim says.

claim: Telling an LLM that an earlier draft is wrong, or having it verify the draft correctly, does not remove the draft's pull on later answers. Removing or filtering the draft text recovers most, not all, of the loss.
agent_test: On drop of a hypothesis, compare three arms at equal tokens: annotate as wrong, annotate plus replacement cause, delete the text and re-derive from remaining facts. Score lingering use of the dropped claim. Contextual drag numbers: GPT-OSS-20B HMMT25 58.63 clean, 20.54 with draft, 42.26 with verification, 45.83 with FILTER; GPQA 46.97, 16.86, 26.66, 43.70.

claim: Retracting a refuted hypothesis together with the conclusions built on it beats deleting only the refuted item (navigation agent: SR 72.41 full, 70.85 local delete only, 68.61 without cascade).
agent_test: Keep a dependency list per hypothesis; on drop, invalidate dependents; compare to drop-only on a multi-step diagnosis task.

claim: No study gives a validated count threshold for reframing. Candidate triggers with some support: graded confidence loss that grows with the amount and variety of anomalous cues (humans, Hemmerich 2016); a streak of 2 low-confidence turns plus a cooldown of 3 (agent default, not tuned, misfires on transient dips); a mismatch between a written expected outcome and the observation (EVU, 49.8 vs 46.3 for generic reflection); repeated retry of a failed call (44-76% of next actions).
agent_test: Compare triggers at equal tokens: (a) streak>=2, (b) expected-vs-observed mismatch, (c) repeat-failure, (d) never. Score time to reframe, false reframes on transient noise, final accuracy.

claim: Agents under-diagnose tool or source anomalies and keep patching: with recovery paths available, hints that name the hazard recover 60-80% of the lost accuracy, while more test-time thinking helps less; 48.6% of failed trajectories were ineffective continuation.
agent_test: Add an operator that fires after a repeated failed action and asks 'what could be wrong with the source, not the call'.

claim: LLM agents often notice a conflict in a tool return and still pass the corrupted content on (warning in 4.2% of adopting answers). This is the LLM form of explaining away. An LLM judge using the rule 'explicit statement that a return is wrong, suspicious, implausible or conflicting' can detect the noticed-but-passed-through pattern in traces.
agent_test: Log noticed-conflict statements and whether the final answer used the flagged value; target zero adoption of flagged values.

claim: Withholding the commit slot works better than telling the model to wait: deferring the diagnostic question raised first-commit accuracy by up to 62.6%, and holding back salient lab evidence prevented an accuracy loss of up to 23.3%.
agent_test: Keep the agent in an open state with no stated leading hypothesis until a minimum evidence set is collected; compare with an instruction to wait.

claim: Clarify/abstain operators have a time window: goal clarification loses nearly all value after 10% of a run (pass@3 0.78 to baseline) while input clarification keeps value to about 50%; late clarification is worse than never asking. A trajectory-distilled stopping rule raised timely abstention from 26.7 to 57.4 on WebShop but its cost on answerable tasks was not measured.
agent_test: Paired tasks (should-act and should-abstain); ask goal questions in the first tenth of a run; report cost on the should-act side.
audit_note: Minor: the 0.78 vs 0.40 no-clarification gap is from only 18 goal variants, late-is-worse-than-never applies to deferral past mid-trajectory, and the 26.7 to 57.4 figure is Llama-3.3-70B only on an abstention-only WebShop subset.

claim: Forced disconfirming tests have not been tested outside rule games: the only LLM evidence is correlational across models (rho -0.779 between positive-test share and success).
agent_test: Diagnosis task where the leading hypothesis predicts a specific test will fail; require that test; compare with free testing at equal tokens.
